newsitem.title: BELGIUM: The further the rise, the deeper the OLO correction.
newsitem.headline: The further the rise, the deeper the OLO correction.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and futures, pausing for breath on Tuesday, have further headway to make now that stock markets are approaching overbought levels, some Belgian dealers said.
"There is little to counter the upsurge," one trader said, citing an environment where interest rates and inflation remain low and economies grow heathily.

Others, however, said the upside was limited with all the good news discounted. At seven basis points the 10-year yield spread over Bunds was about as low as it could be given the difference between the Belgian and the German credit risk.

"One wonders if a correction will come at all. Investors are stuck in an unpleasant position. Bonds yield less by the day and there is still so much money left. It looks as if markets are waiting for a bull trap, i.e. everybody needs to be invested before the correction begins," ABN AMRO said on ABKR.
A Belgian bank trader said, "There will not be a major correction yet. The future looks rosy. There are no alternatives for bonds, really. Shares are no longer the market's darling."
Despite the fact that the spread widened slightly from six bps in the course of the day as Bunds recovered more rapidly than OLOs, he said the market was "solid" versus Bunds.
He said the seven- to eight-year area, particularly OLO 14 BE265= and OLO 19 BE273=, was expensive at the moment, but he was hard pressed to find cheaper issues.
